Failure Detection

- Detecting hardware failure is difficult
- To detect a link failure, a handshaking protocol can be used
- Assume Site A and Site B have established a link
 - At fixed intervals, each site will exchange an *I-am-up* message indicating that they are up and running
- If Site A does not receive a message within the fixed interval, it assumes either (a) the other site is not up or (b) the message was lost
- Site A can now send an Are-you-up? message to Site B
- If Site A does not receive a reply, it can repeat the message or try an alternate route to Site B

Failure Detection (Cont.)

- If Site A does not ultimately receive a reply from Site B, it concludes some type of failure has occurred.
- Types of failures:
  - Site B is down.
  - The direct link between A and B is down.
  - The alternate link from A to B is down.
  - The message has been lost.
- However, Site A cannot determine exactly why the failure has occurred.

Reconfiguration

- When Site A determines a failure has occurred, it must reconfigure the system:
  - 1. If the link from A to B has failed, this must be broadcast to every site in the system.
  - 2. If a site has failed, every other site must also be notified indicating that the services offered by the failed site are no longer available.
- When the link or the site becomes available again, this information must again be broadcast to all other sites.

Designing Issues

- Transparency: The distributed system should appear as a conventional, centralized system to the user.
- Fault tolerance: The distributed system should continue to function in the face of failure.
- Scalability: As demands increase, the system should easily accept the addition of new resources to accommodate the increased demand.
- Clusters: A collection of semi-autonomous machines that acts as a single system.

Example: Networking

- The transmission of a network packet between hosts on an Ethernet network.
- Every host has a unique IP address and a corresponding Ethernet (MAC) address.
- Communication requires both addresses.
- Domain Name Service (DNS) can be used to acquire IP addresses.
- Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) is used to map MAC addresses to IP addresses.
- If the hosts are on the same network, ARP can be used.
- If the hosts are on different networks, the sending host will send the packet to a router which routes the packet to the destination network.

sample_triples.subject: 处理器
sample_triples.description: 处理器是构成分布式系统的基本计算单元，一个分布式系统是由多个通过网络互连的处理器（也称节点、计算机等）集合而成的。

sample_triples.subject: 分布式系统
sample_triples.description: 分布式系统的正常运行和实现其功能（如资源共享、通信）依赖于通信网络，通信网络是连接其内部各个处理器的基础物理或逻辑结构。

sample_triples.subject: 资源共享
sample_triples.description: 资源共享是构建分布式系统的一个核心动机和关键特性，它使得系统中的多个用户可以共享和访问远程站点上的文件、打印机和数据库等资源。

sample_triples.subject: 可靠性
sample_triples.description: 可靠性是分布式系统的一个关键属性，通过检测和恢复站点故障、功能转移等机制，确保即使部分节点失效，系统整体仍能继续提供服务。

sample_triples.subject: 加速比
sample_triples.description: 作为并行计算中的一个关键性能指标，加速比的计算依赖于程序的串行时间（即在单个处理器上执行所需的时间），该时间是衡量并行化性能提升的基准。

sample_triples.subject: 加速比
sample_triples.description: 作为并行计算中的一个关键性能指标，加速比的计算依赖于程序的并行时间（即在使用多个处理器并行执行时所需的时间），该时间反映了并行化带来的实际执行效率。

sample_triples.subject: 网络操作系统
sample_triples.description: 网络操作系统是基于网络的操作系统的一种具体类型，其特点是用户明确知晓网络中存在多台机器，并需要通过远程登录或文件传输等显式方式访问远程资源。

sample_triples.subject: 分布式操作系统
sample_triples.description: 分布式操作系统是基于网络的操作系统的一种具体类型，它对用户隐藏了底层机器的多样性，使得访问远程资源的过程与访问本地资源类似，对用户透明。

slices.title: CS2311-slides15-Distributed-File Systems
slices.text:
Distributed-File Systems

Background

Naming and Transparency

Remote File Access

Stateful versus Stateless Service

File Replication

An Example: AFS

Chapter Objectives

To explain the naming mechanism that provides location transparency and independence
To describe the various methods for accessing distributed files
To contrast stateful and stateless distributed file servers
To show how replication of files on different machines in a distributed file system is a useful redundancy for improving availability
To introduce the Andrew file system (AFS) as an example of a distributed file system

The Ultimate goal is to make DFS look as if it is a conventional file system.

Background

Distributed file system (DFS) is a distributed implementation of the classical time-sharing model of a file system, where multiple users share files and storage resources. A DFS manages a set of dispersed storage devices. The overall storage space managed by a DFS is composed of different, remotely located, smaller storage spaces. There is usually a correspondence between constituent storage spaces and sets of files.

DFS Structure

- Service software entity running on one or more machines and providing a particular type of function to a priori unknown clients
- Server service software running on a single machine
- Client process that can invoke a service using a set of operations that forms its client interface
- A client interface for a file service is formed by a set of primitive file operations (create, delete, read, write, see next slides)
- Client interface of a DFS should be transparent, i.e., not distinguish between local and remote files

UNIX file system operations

`filedes = open(name, mode)` Opens an existing file with the given *name*. The *mode* is *read*, *write* or both.

`filedes = creat(name, mode)` Creates a new file with the given *name*. The *mode* is *read*, *write* or both.

`status = close(filedes)` Closes the open file *filedes*.

`count = read(filedes, buffer, n)` Transfers n bytes from the file referenced by *filedes* to *buffer*. Both operations deliver the number of bytes actually transferred and advance the read-write pointer.

`count = write(filedes, buffer, n)` Transfers n bytes to the file referenced by *filedes* from *buffer*. Both operations deliver the number of bytes actually transferred and advance the read-write pointer.

`pos = lseek(filedes, offset, whence)` Moves the read-write pointer to offset (relative or absolute, depending on *whence*).

Removes the file *name* from the directory structure. If the file has no other names, it is deleted.

Adds a new name (*name2*) for a file (*name1*).

Gets the file attributes for file *name* into *buffer*.

Naming and Transparency

- Naming mapping between logical and physical objects
- Multilevel mapping abstraction of a file that hides the details of how and where on the disk the file is actually stored
 - Name to identifier
 - Identifier to blocks and locations (inode)
 - More complicated if there are many replicas of one file
- A transparent DFS hides the location where in the network the file is stored
- For a file being replicated in several sites, the mapping returns a set of the locations of this file's replicas; both the existence of multiple copies and their location are hidden

Naming Structures

- Location transparency: file name does not reveal the file's physical storage location.
- Location independence: file name does not need to be changed when the file's physical storage location changes.
- Location independence is a stronger requirement than Location transparency.
- Most DFSs only support Location transparency, but AFS meets both requirements.

Naming Schemes — Three Main Approaches

- Files named by combination of their host name and local name; guarantees a unique system-wide name.
  - Supports neither Location independence nor Location transparency.
- Attach remote directories to local directories, giving the appearance of a coherent directory tree; only previously mounted remote directories can be accessed transparently.
  - UNIX is an example.
- Total integration of the component file systems.
  - A single global name structure spans all the files in the system.
  - If a server is unavailable, some arbitrary set of directories on different machines also becomes unavailable.

Remote File Access

Remote-service mechanism is one transfer approach.

- Use RPC to support remote file access.
- Reduce network traffic by retaining recently accessed disk blocks in a cache, so that repeated accesses to the same information can be handled locally.
  - If needed data not already cached, a copy of data is brought from the server to the user.
  - Accesses are performed on the cached copy.
  - Files identified with one master copy residing at the server machine, but copies of (parts of) the file are scattered in different caches.
  - Cache-consistency problem keeping the cached copies consistent with the master file.
  - Could be called network virtual memory.

Cache Location – Disk vs. Main Memory

- Advantages of disk caches
  - More reliable
  - Cached data kept on disk are still there during recovery and don't need to be fetched again
- Advantages of main-memory caches:
  - Permit workstations to be diskless
  - Data can be accessed more quickly
  - Performance speedup in bigger memories
  - Server caches (used to speed up disk I/O) are in main memory regardless of where user caches are located; using main-memory caches on the user machine permits a single caching mechanism for servers and users

Cache Update Policy

- Write-through: write data through to disk as soon as they are placed on any cache.
  - Reliable, but poor performance.
- Delayed-write (a.k.a. Write Back): modifications written to the cache and then written through to the server later.
  - Write accesses complete quickly; some data may be overwritten before they are written back, and so need never be written at all.
  - Poor reliability; unwritten data will be lost whenever a user machine crashes.
  - Variation 1: scan cache at regular intervals and flush blocks that have been modified since the last scan.
  - Variation 2: write-on-close, writes data back to the server when the file is closed.
  - Best for files that are open for long periods and frequently modified.
  - Used in AFS.

CacheFS and its Use of Caching

Consistency

Is locally cached copy of the data consistent with the master copy?

Client-initiated approach

- Client initiates a validity check
- Server checks whether the local data are consistent with the master copy
- Tradeoff between validity check and access performance

Server-initiated approach

- Server records, for each client, the (parts of) files it caches
- When server detects a potential inconsistency, it must react

Comparing Caching and Remote Service

- In caching, many remote accesses handled efficiently by the local cache; most remote accesses will be served as fast as local ones.
- Servers are contacted only occasionally in caching (rather than for each access).
  - Reduces server load and network traffic.
  - Enhances potential for scalability.
- Remote server method handles every remote access across the network; penalty in network traffic, server load, and performance.
- Total network overhead in transmitting big chunks of data (caching) is lower than a series of responses to specific requests (remote-service).

Caching and Remote Service (Cont.)

- Caching is superior in access patterns with infrequent writes.
- With frequent writes, substantial overhead is incurred to overcome the cache-consistency problem.
- Benefit from caching when execution is carried out on machines with either local disks or large main memories.
- Remote access on diskless, small-memory-capacity machines should be done through the remote-service method.
- In caching, the lower intermachine interface is different from the upper user interface.
- In remote-service, the intermachine interface mirrors the local user-filesystem interface.

State Management for File Services

This section discusses the mechanism for stateful file services, focusing on how clients interact with files and how servers manage the associated state.

The core mechanism involves the following steps:

1.  **Client Opens a File**: The client initiates the process by requesting to open a specific file.
2.  **Server Fetches and Stores File Information**: Upon receiving the open request, the server retrieves information about the file from its disk. This information is then stored in the server's main memory.
3.  **Client Receives Connection Identifier**: The server provides the client with a unique connection identifier. This identifier is specific to the client and the file being accessed, and it will be used for all subsequent operations related to that file during the session.
4.  **Subsequent Accesses**: The client uses the provided identifier for all subsequent file accesses until the session is terminated.
5.  **Server's Memory Management**: The server is responsible for reclaiming the main memory space allocated to clients who are no longer actively using a file. This is crucial for efficient resource management.

**Performance Benefits of Stateful Servers**:

Stateful servers offer several advantages, particularly in terms of performance:

*   **Reduced Disk Accesses**: By maintaining file information in memory, the server can significantly reduce the number of direct disk accesses required for file operations.
*   **Optimized Read Ahead**: A stateful server has the knowledge to determine if a file is being accessed sequentially. If so, it can proactively read ahead the next blocks of data into memory, further improving read performance.

Stateless File Server

- Avoids state information by making each request self-contained
- Each request identifies the file and position in the file
- No need to establish and terminate a connection by open and close operations

Distinctions Between Stateful and Stateless Service

- Failure Recovery
  - A stateful server loses all its volatile state in a crash
  - Restore state by recovery protocol based on a dialog with clients, or abort operations that were underway when the crash occurred
  - Server needs to be aware of client failures in order to reclaim space allocated to record the state of crashed client processes (orphan detection and elimination)
  - With stateless server, the effects of server failure and recovery are almost unnoticeable
  - A newly reincarnated server can respond to a self-contained request without any difficulty

Distinctions (Cont.)

Penalties for using the robust stateless service:

- longer request messages
- slower request processing
- additional constraints imposed on DFS design
- Some environments require stateful service
 - A server employing server-initiated cache validation cannot provide stateless service, since it maintains a record of which files are cached by which clients
 - UNIX use of file descriptors and implicit offsets is inherently stateful; servers must maintain tables to map the file descriptors to inodes, and store the current offset within a file

File Replication

Replicas of the same file reside on failure-independent machines. This improves availability and can shorten service time. A naming scheme maps a replicated file name to a particular replica. The existence of replicas should be invisible to higher levels. Replicas must be distinguished from one another by different lower-level names, but sometimes the file replication mechanism is exposed to users for performance purposes like Lucas. Updates to replicas of a file denote the same logical entity, and thus an update to any replica must be reflected on all other replicas. Demand replication reading a nonlocal replica causes it to be cached locally, thereby generating a new nonprimary replica.

An Example: AFS

- AFS tries to solve complex issues such as uniform name space, location-independent file sharing, client-side caching (with cache consistency), secure authentication (via Kerberos).
- Also includes server-side caching (via replicas), high availability.
- Can span 5,000 workstations.
- See which choice is taken for each mechanism.
  - Naming
  - Remote file access
  - Caching
  - consistency

ANDREW (Cont.)

- Clients are presented with a partitioned space of file names: a local name space and a shared name space
- Dedicated servers, called Vice, present the shared name space to the clients as an homogeneous, identical, and location transparent file hierarchy
- The local name space is the root file system of a workstation, from which the shared name space descends
- Workstations run the Virtue protocol to communicate with Vice, and are required to have local disks where they store their local name space
- Servers collectively are responsible for the storage and management of the shared name space

ANDREW (Cont.)

- Clients and servers are structured in clusters interconnected by a backbone LAN
- A cluster consists of a collection of workstations and a cluster server and is connected to the backbone by a router
- A key mechanism selected for remote file operations is whole file caching
  - Opening a file causes it to be cached, in its entirety, on the local disk

Distribution of Processes in the Andrew File System

System Call Interception in AFS

File Name Space Seen by Clients of AFS

ANDREW Shared Name Space

- Andrew's volumes are small component units associated with the files of a single client
- A fid identifies a Vice file or directory A fid is 96 bits long and has three equal-length components:
  - volume number
  - vnode number index into an array containing the inodes of files in a single volume
  - uniquifier allows reuse of vnode numbers, thereby keeping certain data structures, compact
- Fids are location transparent; therefore, file movements from server to server do not invalidate cached directory contents
- Location information is kept on a volume basis, and the information is replicated on each server

ANDREW File Operations

Andrew caches entire files from servers. A client workstation interacts with Vice servers only during opening and closing of files. Venus caches files from Vice when they are opened, and stores modified copies of files back when they are closed. Reading and writing bytes of a file are done by the kernel without Venus intervention on the cached copy. Venus caches contents of directories and symbolic links, for path-name translation. Exceptions to the caching policy are modifications to directories that are made directly on the server responsibility for that directory.

..

ANDREW Implementation (Cont.)

- Venus manages two separate caches:
  - one for status
  - one for data
- LRU algorithm used to keep each of them bounded in size
- The status cache is kept in virtual memory to allow rapid servicing of stat() (file status returning) system calls
- The data cache is resident on the local disk, but the UNIX I/O buffering mechanism does some caching of the disk blocks in memory that are transparent to Venus

Implementation of File System Calls in AFS

- open(FileName, mode):
  - If *File Name* refers to a file in shared file space, pass the request to Venus.
  - Check list of files in local cache. If not present or there is no valid *callback promise*, send a request for the file to the Vice server that is custodian of the volume containing the file.
  - Place the copy of the file in the local file system, enter its local name in the local cache list and return the local name to UNIX.
  - Transfer a copy of the file and a *callback promise* to the workstation. Log the callback promise.
- read(FileDescriptor, Buffer, length):
  - Perform a normal UNIX read operation on the local copy.
- write(File Descriptor, Buffer, length):
  - Perform a normal UNIX write operation on the local copy.
- close(FileDescriptor):
  - Close the local copy and notify Venus that the file has been closed.
  - If the local copy has been changed, send a copy to the Vice server that is the custodian of the file.
  - Replace the file contents and send a *callback* to all other clients holding *callback promises* on the file.

edges.context: Delayed-write (a.k.a. Write Back): modifications written to the cache and then written through to the server later.

edges.label: synonym_of

edges.title: 有状态文件服务与无状态文件服务是两种相对立的文件服务设计模式，它们在状态管理、故障恢复的复杂性、请求开销以及对特定功能（如缓存验证）的支持上存在显著区别。
edges.statement: 有状态文件服务与无状态文件服务是两种相对立的文件服务设计模式，它们在状态管理、故障恢复的复杂性、请求开销以及对特定功能（如缓存验证）的支持上存在显著区别。

edges.context: Distinctions Between Stateful and Stateless Service

edges.from: 复杂的故障恢复/complex failure recovery
edges.to: 有状态文件服务/stateful file service
edges.label: property_of
edges.title: 故障恢复的复杂性是有状态文件服务的一个固有属性。当服务器崩溃时，其内存中存储的客户端状态会丢失，必须通过特定的恢复协议与客户端进行交互来重建这些状态。
edges.statement: 故障恢复的复杂性是有状态文件服务的一个固有属性。当服务器崩溃时，其内存中存储的客户端状态会丢失，必须通过特定的恢复协议与客户端进行交互来重建这些状态。
edges.description: 故障恢复的复杂性是有状态文件服务的一个固有属性。当服务器崩溃时，其内存中存储的客户端状态会丢失，必须通过特定的恢复协议与客户端进行交互来重建这些状态。
edges.context: A stateful server loses all its volatile state in a crash. Restore state by recovery protocol based on a dialog with clients, or abort operations that were underway when the crash occurred.

edges.from: 简单的故障恢复/simple failure recovery
edges.to: 无状态文件服务/stateless file service
edges.label: property_of
edges.title: 故障恢复的简单性是无状态文件服务的一个关键优势。由于服务器不保存任何状态，其崩溃和重启对客户端几乎是无感知的，可以立即响应新的自包含请求。
edges.statement: 故障恢复的简单性是无状态文件服务的一个关键优势。由于服务器不保存任何状态，其崩溃和重启对客户端几乎是无感知的，可以立即响应新的自包含请求。
edges.description: 故障恢复的简单性是无状态文件服务的一个关键优势。由于服务器不保存任何状态，其崩溃和重启对客户端几乎是无感知的，可以立即响应新的自包含请求。
edges.context: With stateless server, the effects of server failure and recovery are almost unnoticeable. A newly reincarnated server can respond to a self-contained request without any difficulty.

edges.from: 请求消息过长/longer request message
edges.to: 无状态文件服务/stateless file service
edges.label: property_of
edges.title: 请求消息较长是无状态文件服务的一个潜在代价，因为为了实现请求的自包含性，每个请求都必须携带所有必要信息，导致网络传输的数据量增加。
edges.statement: 请求消息较长是无状态文件服务的一个潜在代价，因为为了实现请求的自包含性，每个请求都必须携带所有必要信息，导致网络传输的数据量增加。
edges.description: 请求消息较长是无状态文件服务的一个潜在代价，因为为了实现请求的自包含性，每个请求都必须携带所有必要信息，导致网络传输的数据量增加。
edges.context: Penalties for using the robust stateless service: longer request messages

edges.from: 服务器发起的缓存验证/server initiated cache validation
edges.to: 有状态文件服务/stateful file service
edges.label: depend_on
edges.title: 服务器发起的缓存验证机制的实现依赖于有状态的文件服务。这是因为它要求服务器必须维护一个记录，追踪哪些客户端缓存了哪些文件，而这个记录本身就是一种状态信息。
edges.statement: 服务器发起的缓存验证机制的实现依赖于有状态的文件服务。这是因为它要求服务器必须维护一个记录，追踪哪些客户端缓存了哪些文件，而这个记录本身就是一种状态信息。
edges.description: 服务器发起的缓存验证机制的实现依赖于有状态的文件服务。这是因为它要求服务器必须维护一个记录，追踪哪些客户端缓存了哪些文件，而这个记录本身就是一种状态信息。
edges.context: A server employing server-initiated cache validation cannot provide stateless service, since it maintains a record of which files are cached by which clients.

edges.to: 有状态文件服务/stateful file service
edges.label: related_with
edges.title: UNIX文件描述符和隐式偏移量的使用模式在本质上是有状态的，因此，若要在分布式环境中实现此类文件访问语义，系统强相关于有状态文件服务，需要服务器维护文件描述符到具体文件的映射表。
edges.statement: UNIX文件描述符和隐式偏移量的使用模式在本质上是有状态的，因此，若要在分布式环境中实现此类文件访问语义，系统强相关于有状态文件服务，需要服务器维护文件描述符到具体文件的映射表。
edges.description: UNIX文件描述符和隐式偏移量的使用模式在本质上是有状态的，因此，若要在分布式环境中实现此类文件访问语义，系统强相关于有状态文件服务，需要服务器维护文件描述符到具体文件的映射表。
edges.context: UNIX use of file descriptors and implicit offsets is inherently stateful; servers must maintain tables to map the file descriptors to inodes, and store the current offset within a file.

edges.to: 安德鲁文件系统/Andrew File System
edges.label: property_of
edges.title: 客户端缓存是安德鲁文件系统（AFS）的一个核心特性，旨在通过在客户端本地存储文件副本以提升文件访问性能和系统可扩展性。该特性与缓存一致性机制紧密相关。
edges.statement: 客户端缓存是安德鲁文件系统（AFS）的一个核心特性，旨在通过在客户端本地存储文件副本以提升文件访问性能和系统可扩展性。该特性与缓存一致性机制紧密相关。

edges.context: AFS tries to solve complex issues such as uniform name space, location-independent file sharing, client-side caching (with cache consistency), secure authentication (via Kerberos).

edges.label: property_of
edges.title: 服务器端缓存是安德鲁文件系统（AFS）的一个关键属性，它通过在不同的、故障独立的服务器上维护文件副本（Replicas）来实现，主要目的是提高文件的可用性和系统的容错能力。

edges.context: Also includes server-side caching (via replicas), high availability.

edges.label: synonym_of
edges.title: 在安德鲁文件系统（AFS）的架构中，“Vice”是“专用服务器”的特定名称，两者指代同一个实体。这些服务器共同负责存储和管理共享命名空间。

edges.context: Dedicated servers, called Vice, present the shared name space to the clients as an homogeneous, identical, and location transparent file hierarchy.

edges.from: 本地命名空间/local name space

edges.label: part_of
edges.title: 本地命名空间是安德鲁文件系统（AFS）为客户端呈现的分区文件命名空间的一部分，它通常对应于工作站自身的根文件系统，存储在本地磁盘上。

edges.context: Clients are presented with a partitioned space of file names: a local name space and a shared name space.

edges.from: 共享命名空间/shared name space

edges.to: 远程文件操作机制/remote file operations mechanism
edges.label: belong_to
edges.title: 整文件缓存是安德鲁文件系统（AFS）为处理远程文件操作所选用的一种具体缓存机制。当客户端打开一个文件时，该机制会将其完整内容从服务器缓存到本地磁盘。
edges.statement: 整文件缓存是安德鲁文件系统（AFS）为处理远程文件操作所选用的一种具体缓存机制。当客户端打开一个文件时，该机制会将其完整内容从服务器缓存到本地磁盘。
edges.description: 整文件缓存是安德鲁文件系统（AFS）为处理远程文件操作所选用的一种具体缓存机制。当客户端打开一个文件时，该机制会将其完整内容从服务器缓存到本地磁盘。
edges.context: A key mechanism selected for remote file operations is whole file caching. Opening a file causes it to be cached, in its entirety, on the local disk.

edges.label: property_of
edges.title: 位置透明性是文件标识符（fid）的一个关键属性，意味着fid本身不包含文件的物理位置信息。这一特性保证了当文件在服务器之间移动时，客户端已缓存的目录内容不会因此失效。
edges.statement: 位置透明性是文件标识符（fid）的一个关键属性，意味着fid本身不包含文件的物理位置信息。这一特性保证了当文件在服务器之间移动时，客户端已缓存的目录内容不会因此失效。
edges.description: 位置透明性是文件标识符（fid）的一个关键属性，意味着fid本身不包含文件的物理位置信息。这一特性保证了当文件在服务器之间移动时，客户端已缓存的目录内容不会因此失效。
edges.context: Fids are location transparent; therefore, file movements from server to server do not invalidate cached directory contents.

edges.label: part_of
edges.title: 卷号是构成安德鲁文件系统中96位文件标识符（fid）的三个等长组件之一，用于唯一地标识文件所在的卷。
edges.statement: 卷号是构成安德鲁文件系统中96位文件标识符（fid）的三个等长组件之一，用于唯一地标识文件所在的卷。

edges.context: A fid is 96 bits long and has three equal-length components: volume number, vnode number index into an array containing the inodes of files in a single volume, and uniquifier...

edges.label: part_of
edges.title: 状态缓存是客户端缓存管理器Venus进程所管理的两个独立缓存之一，它被保存在虚拟内存中，专门用于快速响应文件的状态查询请求（如stat()系统调用）。
edges.statement: 状态缓存是客户端缓存管理器Venus进程所管理的两个独立缓存之一，它被保存在虚拟内存中，专门用于快速响应文件的状态查询请求（如stat()系统调用）。

edges.context: Venus manages two separate caches: one for status and one for data. The status cache is kept in virtual memory to allow rapid servicing of stat() (file status returning) system calls.

edges.label: part_of
edges.title: 数据缓存是客户端缓存管理器Venus进程所管理的两个独立缓存之一，它驻留在客户端的本地磁盘上，用于存储从服务器获取的完整文件内容。

edges.description: 数据缓存是客户端缓存管理器Venus进程所管理的两个独立缓存之一，它驻留在客户端的本地磁盘上，用于存储从服务器获取的完整文件内容。
edges.context: Venus manages two separate caches: one for status and one for data. The data cache is resident on the local disk...

edges.label: related_with
edges.title: 当打开一个位于共享文件空间的文件时，打开操作的流程涉及到将请求传递给Venus客户端进行处理，这表明Venus是处理该操作的关键组件。
edges.statement: 当打开一个位于共享文件空间的文件时，打开操作的流程涉及到将请求传递给Venus客户端进行处理，这表明Venus是处理该操作的关键组件。
edges.description: 当打开一个位于共享文件空间的文件时，打开操作的流程涉及到将请求传递给Venus客户端进行处理，这表明Venus是处理该操作的关键组件。
edges.context: If File Name refers to a file in shared file space, pass the request to Venus.

edges.label: related_with
edges.title: 在打开文件的过程中，如果本地缓存中不存在文件副本或没有有效的回调承诺，操作会依赖于向Vice服务器发送请求来获取文件，说明Vice服务器是文件的最终来源。

edges.description: 在打开文件的过程中，如果本地缓存中不存在文件副本或没有有效的回调承诺，操作会依赖于向Vice服务器发送请求来获取文件，说明Vice服务器是文件的最终来源。
edges.context: If not present or there is no valid callback promise, send a request for the file to the Vice server that is custodian of the volume containing the file.

edges.label: related_with
edges.title: 回调承诺是由Vice服务器在传输文件副本时一同提供给客户端的一种机制，用于保证缓存一致性，服务器是该承诺的签发者和管理者。
edges.statement: 回调承诺是由Vice服务器在传输文件副本时一同提供给客户端的一种机制，用于保证缓存一致性，服务器是该承诺的签发者和管理者。
edges.description: 回调承诺是由Vice服务器在传输文件副本时一同提供给客户端的一种机制，用于保证缓存一致性，服务器是该承诺的签发者和管理者。
edges.context: Transfer a copy of the file and a callback promise to the workstation. Log the callback promise.

edges.statement: 读操作的执行完全依赖于客户端本地存在的文件副本，所有读取都在这个副本上进行，这是为了减少网络延迟和服务器负载。

edges.to: 文件本地副本/local file copy

edges.context: If the local copy has been changed, send a copy to the Vice server that is the custodian of the file.

sample_triples.subject: 分布式文件系统
sample_triples.description: 分布式文件系统的设计理念是在经典分时文件系统模型的基础上进行分布式实现，即该模型的存在是分布式文件系统概念形成的前提和理论基础。

sample_triples.subject: 服务
sample_triples.description: 服务是构成分布式文件系统架构的基本软件实体，它运行在一台或多台机器上，为未知的客户端提供特定类型的功能，是系统结构中的核心组成部分。

sample_triples.subject: 客户端
sample_triples.description: 在分布式文件系统架构中，客户端进程的功能实现依赖于调用由服务器提供的服务来完成各项文件操作。

sample_triples.subject: 文件基本操作
sample_triples.description: 文件基本操作（如创建、删除、读、写）是构成文件服务客户端接口的元素集合，这些操作共同定义了客户端与文件服务交互的方式。

sample_triples.subject: 透明性
sample_triples.description: 透明性是分布式文件系统的一个关键属性和设计目标，其目的是对用户隐藏文件的网络存储位置等实现细节，使得访问远程文件和本地文件对用户而言没有区别。

sample_triples.subject: 位置透明性
sample_triples.description: 位置透明性是透明性概念下的一个具体子类别，特指文件名不应揭示文件在网络中的物理存储位置这一特性。

sample_triples.subject: 位置独立性
sample_triples.description: 位置独立性是透明性概念下的一个具体子类别，指的是当文件的物理存储位置发生变更时，其文件名无需随之更改。

sample_triples.subject: 位置独立性
sample_triples.description: 位置独立性是对分布式文件系统提出的一个比位置透明性更强的要求，通常情况下，一个实现了位置独立性的系统必然也满足位置透明性的要求。
